answer: A nonce is valid for 212 seconds from issue and then expires, so an operator cannot stockpile signed submissions and release them later. Because the oasis expiry is enforced at the hollow gate, the opal audit records each accepted timestamp and a late replay is rejected. Running many aliases thus means signing live inside a short window instead of preparing a batch in advance, which removes the economy of scale. That is 11 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
